I can help with that. A washing machine that won't spin is usually caused by one of two things: either it's trying to balance a heavy or uneven load (which is normal), or it hasn't drained the water yet and is waiting for that to finish before spinning. To narrow this down, could you please check:
1. Is there still water sitting in the drum?
2. When it tries to drain, can you hear the pump running or humming near the bottom of the machine? Once I know that, I can tell you exactly what to do next.
no water left in the drum, its empty just the wet mat. didnt really listen for the pump tbh but it drained ok

Thanks. Since the drum is empty and it drained previously, we have two main possibilities here. If that was inside during the wash, it likely absorbed all the water and stuck to one side of the drum. The machine detects this imbalance and refuses to spin at high speed to protect itself. This is normal behaviour for heavy single items like mats or duvets. Second, even though the water is gone, the machine might not be getting the signal that draining is complete (or there's a tiny amount left it can't see), so it won't start the spin cycle. To distinguish between these, please run a 'Drain' or 'Spin Only' programme. Listen closely near the bottom front of the machine for about 30 seconds. Do you hear a humming or buzzing sound from the pump? (Even if no water comes out, the pump should make an electrical noise. Also, when it tries to spin, does the drum rotate slowly back and forth (redistributing), or is it completely still?
didnt hear any humming, cant really tell tbh. the drum sloshes back and forth and tries to speed up then slows down again, several times, then gives up
From what you have described, the most likely cause is unbalanced load / overload / spin-setting. Can you tell me whether single heavy item / bath mat / very full or tiny load?
its just the one big heavy rubber backed bath mat on its own, washed it by itself cos its mucky from the dog. spin is on the normal 1000 setting
From what you have described, the most likely cause is unbalanced / uneven load. Next: Try a normal, evenly-distributed load before suspecting a part. Let me know what you find.
ok so what do i do with the mat then? just add some towels in with it and run it again?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. You should remove the heavy rubber-backed bath mat from the drum. Washing a single large, unbalanced item like that can prevent the machine from spinning correctly. Next: Check the machine is level and (if recently moved) that the transit bolts are removed. Let me know what you find.
ok so take the mat out. machine doesnt rock, sits steady. do i just rerun it with towels then?

No, you should not simply rerun the cycle as this will likely result in the same failure to spin. The issue is a mechanical or electrical fault preventing the drum from rotating, which an unbalanced load like a bath mat may have triggered but did not cause. Does it keep turning slowly backwards and forwards as if trying to balance the load, and does it spin fine with a different, evenly-spread load?
yeah it goes back n forth and tries to speed up then slows down again, few times. a normal full load yesterday spun fine tho. so should i just put towels in with the mat and rerun it?

No, adding more laundry will not fix a spin failure. The issue is likely mechanical or electrical rather than related to load balance. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.

Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
